title: Driving with Autonomous Aids
description: EEG dataset from a semi-automated driving task designed to study human trust in automation (TiA). Participants performed lane maintenance, following-distance control, and pedestrian collision avoidance, with an optional automated assistant of varying quality that they could engage or disengage. Physiological (EEG, EOG, ECG, EDA, gaze) and behavioral measures were recorded to develop metrics that index and predict trust-based decisions.
methods_description: Participants completed a simulated driving task under several conditions: practice, manual driving, and full or speed-only autonomy with good or bad reliability. Drivers could engage or disengage the automated assistant at will and responded to pedestrians with button presses. EEG, EOG, ECG, EDA, gaze position and vehicle control behavior were recorded.
